subject: Post-call: HealthSync data handling & short-store exception request
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Kim <lara.kim@healthsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T15:02:00-05:00
Subject: Post-call: HealthSync data handling & short-store exception request

Hi Lara — thanks again for the quick call earlier. Wanted to capture the main points and next steps so we’re aligned.

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary ask: HealthSync needs minimal persistence of LLM request/response data for PCI/PHI screening. Preferred: 0-retention for conversation text.
- Secondary ask: If 0-retention isn’t feasible for certain flows, HealthSync will accept a short-store window (7 days) for logs used only for debugging, with strict access controls and automatic purge.
- Residency: Production inference must run in us-east-1.
- PII handling: Redaction preferred for name/email/SSN tokens before any persistent storage; opportunity to use client-side redaction or Redwood-managed redaction pipeline.
- Audit evidence: HealthSync will need a SOC2 artifact and audit log samples showing purge events for short-store scenarios.

Attachments I uploaded to the thread: security questionnaire PDF (filled summary) and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) draft with milestones.

Proposed Redwood options to discuss next:
1) 0-retention workflow: ephemeral-only KV/cache with no persisted logs; best for highly-sensitive endpoints (we’ll confirm model/session behaviors and confirm feature parity).
2) 7-day short-store pilot: store encrypted logs for 7 days in a dedicated S3 bucket under your account (or our private VPC) with KMS and RBAC limiting access to two named engineers. Purge is automated and we can provide purge event logs.
3) Redaction + minimal telemetry: perform token-level redaction before persistence, store de-identified metrics for quality monitoring.

Next steps I propose:
- HealthSync legal to confirm which of the above approaches are acceptable. If short-store is acceptable, specify whether Redwood-managed KMS or customer KMS is required.
- Redwood to provide SOC2 artifact and a one-page description of purge evidence and logging access controls (I uploaded the questionnaire with answers).
- If HealthSync wants rapid validation, we can spin a 2-week 7-day short-store pilot scoped to a single staging workspace (cost estimate attached in MAP).

If that looks right, can you confirm (a) whether legal accepts a 7-day pilot as an interim step, and (b) who from legal we should loop for the MAP/DocuSign?

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick call if helpful.

—
Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193

Attachments: HealthSync_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (summary stub), Proposed_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (stub)

From: Lara Kim <lara.kim@healthsync.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealthSync Legal <legal@healthsync.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T17:24:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: HealthSync data handling & short-store exception request

Thanks Connor — helpful summary. Quick answers from our side:

- Our legal team prefers 0-retention for any flow that touches PHI. For product reasons, they may accept a time-limited exception for non-PHI flows; we are interested in a 7-day short-store pilot strictly scoped to non-PHI endpoints.
- For PHI flows we need either client-side redaction or guaranteed ephemeral handling with no persisted logs accessible to Redwood engineers.
- KMS: we prefer customer-managed KMS (HealthSync keys) for any persisted artifacts.
- Audit artifacts: please send SOC2 report + an example purge log and an explanation of how purge events are recorded and signed.

Legal flagged two specific items:
1) Who can access logs during the retention window and how is access approved?
2) How are backups/replication handled for short-store artifacts?

We’re willing to sign a MAP for a 2-week 7-day short-store pilot for the non-PHI staging workspace, provided the technical details match what you described (customer KMS, RBAC, automated purge events delivered to our audit S3).

Can Marissa or Aditya coordinate the MAP and technical design? I’ll ask legal to share a single contact for the contract team tomorrow.

Best,
Lara
Lara Kim
Head of Product | HealthSync
lara.kim@healthsync.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T18:05:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: HealthSync acceptance for 7-day pilot (non-PHI) — next steps

Marissa / Aditya — forwarding Lara's note. Key asks from HealthSync: customer-managed KMS for any persisted logs, RBAC limiting access, automated purge with delivered purge logs, and SOC2 artifact. They are willing to run a 2-week pilot on non-PHI staging with a 7-day short-store window.

Suggested internal plan:
- Marissa: lead the MAP + legal coordination (timeline: draft MAP today, send for signature tomorrow).
- Aditya: confirm our purge-event audit format and whether we can produce a signed purge log that satisfies HealthSync legal; confirm support for customer KMS in the staging pilot and any additional configuration steps.
- Connor: I’ll draft a tight technical appendix describing the pilot scope (single workspace, non-PHI endpoints, customer KMS, RBAC list limited to two Redwood SEs, automated purge schedule at day 7, purge event notification into HealthSync audit S3). I’ve attached an initial logging architecture draft — need your quick review.

Timeline target: pilot running by 2026-11-18, 2-week duration, then a joint post-pilot review.

Notes: be explicit in the MAP that Redwood will not access PHI flows and that any access to short-store artifacts is auditable and limited.

—
Connor

Attachments: Logging-Architecture-draft.pdf (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Kim <lara.kim@healthsync.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:18:00-05:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: HealthSync data handling & short-store exception request

Lara — thanks, appreciate the clarity.

We’ll proceed as follows and I’ll send the MAP by end of day:
- Redwood will provision a single staging workspace in us-east-1 with a 7-day short-store window for non-PHI flows.
- We will configure customer-managed KMS (HealthSync key) and deliver an architecture appendix showing where keys are used.
- RBAC: access will be limited to two named Redwood SEs (Connor + 1 backup) and HealthSync will be able to view purge events via a signed JSON delivered to your audit S3 bucket.
- Deliverables before pilot: SOC2 summary, example purge-event log format, MAP for signature, and technical appendix.

Action items:
- Connor: finalize technical appendix and logging purge sample by EOD.
- Aditya: confirm exact audit payload format and whether we can produce signed purge events (deterministic hash + timestamp).
- Lara: please send the legal contact for MAP/DocuSign and confirm the backup SE we should list for RBAC.

If that timeline works I’ll circulate the MAP and include a short acceptance checklist HealthSync legal can sign off on.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0116
